headline_en: Near maximum from the first chord
note_en: It enters at near maximum from the first chord and rises three times to similar levels. It strikes the third the loudest.
After rising to its loudest at the opening, it reaches for near maximum again. It also sustains loud playing longer than Parham and Kanneh-Mason.
The first sound is less soft than in the other two. It keeps the range between quiet and loud small and reaches maximum once more near the end.
At 2:42, it is about 15 seconds shorter than the other two. It opens the softest of the three and sings its loudest in under a minute.
It alone sounds the first chord at its loudest. The driving passage around the one-minute mark is met at nearly the same level.

headline_en: A big drop after the climax
note_en: At 2:01, it runs about 7 seconds longer than the other two. After its loudest strike it drops the most of the three, then climbs again.
It holds loud playing the longest of the three. In under 30 seconds it surges to near maximum again, and around the one-minute mark it strikes its loudest.
facts_en: Academy of St Martin in the Fields

note_en: Even in the quiet passages it doesn't sink as low as the other two. In the later part too, it carries the song along without cutting the level much.
It sinks the quiet passage late in the piece deeper than the other two. From there it rises again to close the song.

headline_en: Strength in the second big passage
note_en: It keeps the first big passage lower than the other two and strikes its loudest in the second.
It reaches near maximum later than the other two. After the climax it settles lower than Midori and Bell and stays soft to the end.
It sinks the middle deep, then builds up steadily, placing the climax later than the other two.

headline_en: Building all the way to the end
note_en: The shape is the same as Seong-Jin Cho's, but about 20 seconds shorter. After sinking deep in the middle, it builds all the way to the end and strikes its loudest at the very end.

headline_en: The most even of the three
note_en: The gap between quiet and loud is the smallest of the three, and the middle sinks the least. It reaches near maximum the earliest and holds it to the end.
At 2:19, it runs more than 20 seconds longer than the other two. It opens softly and sinks the middle deeper than Bavouzet and Thibaudet.
The first sound is the smallest of the three. Around the 30-second mark it steps up a level, stays there for a long while, then surges once.
At 2:01, it is 15 seconds longer than Abbado. The opening doesn't sink as low as in the other two, and it builds for nearly the last 20 seconds.
At 1:46, the shortest of the three. It sinks the lowest at the start and keeps the middle soft too.
At two minutes, it is longer than the other two. It stays soft for over a minute, drops to its smallest just before the surge, then rises.
At 1:37, it is more than 20 seconds shorter than Karajan. It starts to grow about 10 seconds earlier than the other two and surges first.
The first flute is softer than in the other two. After a deep pause early on, it steps up one level at a time to the end.
It sinks the middle song the deepest of the three. The loudest sound is in the returning march, and it ends the softest too.
At 2:52, it runs 11 seconds longer than the other two. Loud playing is brief, and it reaches near maximum later than Yuja Wang and Lang Lang.

headline_en: Matching marches at start and end
note_en: It rises to its loudest in the first march and plays the returning march at the same level. Unlike Shelley, it leaves the ending loud.
The middle song also sinks less than in the other two. It also holds loud playing for the longest time.
It carries the middle third the loudest of the three. Even before the climax it drops the least of the three.
It reaches the climax 18 seconds earlier than Yuja Wang. After the climax it sinks the softest and sets the ending down.
At 1:48, the shortest of the three. It holds loud playing the longest, and the latter part sinks the least.

headline_en: All at once in the last 5 seconds
note_en: The snare drum starts less softly than in the other two. It saves near maximum until 5 seconds before the end, then rises all at once.
After blasting the first theme twice at near maximum, it pulls the relaxed passage back lower than Rogé and Seong-Jin Cho.
It brings out the first melody the softest of the three. The gap between quiet and loud is also the largest of the three.
It brings out the first melody louder than the other two. The gap between quiet and loud is also the smallest, so it flows evenly.
At 4:37, it runs more than 20 seconds longer than the other two. The shape is the same as Thibaudet's, but the first melody is brought out a little louder.

headline_en: Already at maximum by the middle
note_en: It already reaches near maximum in the exact middle. From there it doesn't come down but holds evenly to the end.

headline_en: The second peak one step lower
note_en: At 2:01, it is 13 seconds longer than Rogé. After the first climax, it keeps the second one step lower and finishes less softly than the other two.
It starts the snare drum the softest of the three. It repeats the pattern of building up and then easing back three times.

headline_en: The climax at the end of the first verse
note_en: It alone strikes the climax at the end of the first verse. The ends of the second and third verses are matched at nearly the same level.

headline_en: Building little by little from the start
note_en: It opens the softest of the three. From there it builds little by little and rises to its loudest around the middle.
The first cry is the loudest, and 10 seconds later it drops straight to its smallest level. It sinks the quiet passage the deepest of the three.

headline_en: The deepest dip with every verse
note_en: Each time a new verse begins, it sinks the softest of the three. It puts the loudest sound at the end of the last verse.
Unlike Muti, it sinks only slightly between verses. The gap between quiet and loud is also the smallest.
At 2:20, it is nearly 20 seconds shorter than the other two. The quiet passage doesn't sink as low as with Muti and Levine.
At 6:04, it runs a minute longer than the other two. Its dynamic range is also narrower than Rogé's and Thibaudet's.

headline_en: The climax on the last cry
note_en: Unlike the other two, it places the loudest sound on the last cry. It builds toward the end and bursts out at the very close.
It reaches near maximum in about 30 seconds, while the other two take over two minutes. Forty seconds after the climax it drops to its smallest level, then rises again to finish.

headline_en: Saved until the end, then loud
note_en: It spares loud playing more than the other two and reaches near maximum 20 seconds later than Perlman. After a deep pause in the middle it builds up again.
After pausing it rises loudly again and holds that level to the end. Its loud playing is the longest of the three, and its ending is the least soft.

headline_en: A climax just before the pause
note_en: It alone strikes its loudest just before the pause in the middle. Right after, it sinks deeper than the other two.

headline_en: A mid-piece climax, an even flow
note_en: It alone places the loudest sound in the middle. It carries the front, middle and back at nearly the same level.
